η2..g: 1 Affirmative or emphasizing particle a ἦ μέγα πένθος Ἀχαιΐδα γαῖαν ἱκάνει Il. 1.254. Cf. Il. 1.78, 232, 240, 255, 293, 342, etc.: ἦ μάλα δή σε διδάσκουσιν θεοὶ αὐτοί Od. 1.384. Cf. Od. 2.60, Od. 4.81, 663, 770, Od. 6.278, Od. 10.465, etc. With an ironical tone Il. 1.229: Od. 2.325. With concessive force, it is sure that, yet, although: ἦ καὶ γένει ὕστερος ἦεν Il. 3.215. b Combined with other particles α ἦ μάν Il. 2.370, Il. 13.354, etc. β ἦ μέν Il. 3.430, Il. 5.197, Il. 9.57 (yet to be sure you are young (heightening the preceding qualified praise)), etc.: Od. 10.65, Od. 11.447, Od. 13.425, etc. This combination introducing an oath Il. 1.77, Il. 14.275, Il. 19.109, etc.: Od. 14.160 = Od. 19.305.– ἦ μήν: ἦ μὴν Τρῶές γε κέλονται (I assure you, virtually = although) Il. 7.393. Cf. Il. 2.291. γ ἦ τε Il. 3.56, 366, Il. 5.201, Il. 10.450, etc.: Od. 1.288, Od. 2.62, Od. 12.138, etc. δ ἦ τοι (ἤτοι) Il. 1.68, 140, 211, Il. 2.813, etc.: Od. 1.155, 267, 307, 394, etc. 2 Interrogative particle a Introducing a direct question α ἦ ἐθέλεις . . . ; Il. 1.133. Cf. Il. 1.203, Il. 2.229, Il. 5.349, Il. 8.140, Il. 15.18, Il. 19.343, Il. 20.17, etc.: ἦ καί μοι νεμεσήσεαι; Od. 1.158. Cf. Od. 1.391, Od. 3.251, Od. 4.682, Od. 8.336, Od. 9.405, Od. 10.284, Od. 11.160, etc. β In the first clause in questions in disjunctive form (cf. ἠέ 2): ἦ πού τις νήσων ἦε . . . ; Od. 13.234, etc. γ Introducing a question with disjunctive force: ἦ ἀνθρώπων εἰμὶ σχεδόν; Od. 6.125, etc. b Introducing an indirect question: τόδε εἰπέ, ἦ . . . Od. 16.138.

ηαται.g: 3 pl. pres. ἥατο, 3 pl. impf. ἧμαι.

ηβαιοσ.g: -ή, -όν. 1 Little, inconsiderable, of small worth, few in number: οὔ οἱ ἔνι τρίχες οὐδʼ ἠβαιαί Od. 18.355. Cf. Il. 14.141: Od. 21.288. 2 Absol. in neut. sing. ἠβαιόν a A little space, a short distance: ἐλθόντες ἠ. ἀπὸ σπείους Od. 9.462. Cf. Il. 13.702. b For a short space of time, for a little: οὐκ ἀνάβλησις ἔσσεται οὐδʼ ἠ. Il. 2.380. Cf. Il. 2.386, Il. 13.106. c A little, to a small or trifling extent: οὔ σε χρὴ αἰδοῦς οὐδʼ ἠ. Od. 3.14. Cf. Il. 20.361.

ηβαω.g: [ἥβη.] Acc. sing. masc. pres. pple. ἡβώοντα Il. 9.446. Nom. pl. ἡβώοντες Il. 24.604: Od. 10.6. Nom. fem. ἡβώωσα Od. 5.69. Opt. ἡβώοιμι Il. 7.157, Il. 11.670, Il. 23.629: Od. 14.468, 503. Contr. ἡβῷμι Il. 7.133. 3 sing. aor. subj. ἡβήσῃ Od. 1.41. Pple. ἡβήσας Od. 19.410. Dual masc. ἡβήσαντε Il. 5.550. 1 To be in one's youthful prime, in the vigour of early manhood: ἀνὴρ μάλʼ ἡβῶν Il. 12.382. Cf. Il. 7.133, 157 = Il. 11.670, Il. 9.446, Il. 23.629, Il. 24.565, 604: = Od. 10.6, Od. 14.468, 503, Od. 23.187. Of a flourishing vine Od. 5.69. 2 In aor., to have attained this stage of growth: ἡβήσαντε ἅμʼ Ἀργείοισιν ἑπέσθην Il. 5.550. Cf. Od. 1.41, Od. 19.410.

ηβη.g: -ης, ἡ. 1 Youthful prime, early manhood: ἥβης μέτρον Il. 11.225, τοῦ περ χαριεστάτη ἥ. (in whom youthful manhood shows most . . .) Il. 24.348. Cf. Il. 13.484, Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363, Il. 17.25: Od. 4.668, Od. 10.279, Od. 11.317, Od. 18.217, Od. 19.532, Od. 23.212. 2 The vigour or strength proper to this stage of growth: ὄφρʼ ἥβῃ πεποίθεα Od. 8.181. Cf. Il. 23.432. In reference to an elderly man, bodily vigour, suppleness of frame: οὐδέ τι ἥβης δεύεται Od. 8.136, δέμας ὤφελλε καὶ ἥβην Od. 16.174 (in both cases of Odysseus). 3 Manhood viewed as a stage attained or to be attained: ἥβην ἵξεσθαι Il. 24.728. Cf. Od. 15.366.

ηγαθεοσ.g: -η, -ον [app. ἠγα- = ἀγα- + θεῖος.] Holy, sacred. Like ζάθεος, epithet of places Il. 1.252, Il. 2.722, Il. 6.133, Il. 21.58, 79: Od. 2.308, Od. 4.599, 702 = Od. 5.20, Od. 8.80, Od. 14.180.

ηγεμονευω.g: [ἡγεμών.] 1 To act as guide or pilot, show the way: θεός τις ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 9.142, Od. 10.141. Cf. Od. 17.194. With dat., to guide (a person), show (him) the way: δεῦρό οἱ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 17.372. Cf. Od. 10.445. With cognate acc., to show (the way): ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύσω Od. 6.261, Od. 7.30. Cf. Od. 10.501. 2 To lead the way, act as leader, take the lead: Τηλέμαχος πρόσθʼ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 22.400. With dat.: τοῖσιν ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 3.386, Od. 8.4 = 421, Od. 23.293. With dat. and cognate acc.: τοῖσιν ὁδὸν ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 24.225. Sim.: ὅτʼ ἀνὴρ ὀχετηγὸς ὕδατι ῥόον ἡγεμονεύῃ (guides the flow) Il. 21.258. 3 To lead the way, give a lead, in a course of action: τῇ ἴμεν ᾗ κε σὺ ἡγεμονεύῃς Il. 15.46. 4 To precede a person by an interval of time: Ὀδυσσεὺς ὕστερος, αὐτὰρ Τηλέμαχος πρόσθʼ ἡγεμόνευεν Od. 24.155. 5 To be the leader, commander or chief of. a With genit.: λοκρῶν Il. 2.527, τῆς ἑτέρης [στιχός] Il. 16.179. Cf. Il. 2.540, 552, 645, 657, etc. b With dat.: Τρωσίν Il. 2.816. 6 Absol., to act as chief or leader, lead one's men Il. 13.53, Il. 16.92.

ηγεμων.g: -όνος, ὁ [ἡγέομαι.] 1 A guide or pilot, one who shows the way: ἅμʼ ἡγεμόνʼ ἐσθλὸν ὄπασσον Od. 15.310. Cf. Od. 10.505. 2 A leader, commander or chief: κέλευεν οἷσιν ἕκαστος ἡγεμόνων Il. 4.429. Cf. Il. 2.365, Il. 3.1, Il. 5.38, Il. 9.85, Il. 12.87, etc.

ηγεομαι.g: Fut. ἡγήσομαι Il. 14.374. 3 sing. aor. ἡγήσατο Il. 1.71, Il. 2.867, Il. 12.251, Il. 20.144, etc.: Od. 2.405, Od. 5.192, Od. 14.48, Od. 24.469, etc. 3 dual -άσθην Il. 2.620, 678, 864, 870. Subj. ἡγήσομαι Od. 15.82. 2 sing. opt. ἡγήσαιο Od. 7.22. 3 sing. -αιτο Il. 2.687: Od. 6.114, 300. 3 sing. imp. ἡγησάσθω Il. 9.168. Infin. ἡγήσασθαι Il. 22.101: Od. 10.263, Od. 14.238. (ἐξ-.) 1 To act as guide or pilot, show the way: καὶ ἂν πάϊς ἡγήσαιτο Od. 6.300. Cf. Od. 13.65, Od. 15.82. With dat., to guide (a person), show (him) the way: ἥ οἱ πόλιν ἡγήσαιτο (to the city) Od. 6.114. Cf. Il. 1.71: Od. 7.22. With cognate acc., to show (the way): τὸν ἠνώγεα αὐτὴν ὁδὸν ἡγήσασθαι (to take me by the way by which he had come) Od. 10.263. 2 To lead the way, act as leader, take the lead: ὣς φωνήσας ἡγήσατο Il. 20.144. Cf. Il. 9.168, 192, Il. 12.28, Il. 24.96: Od. 1.125, Od. 2.405 = Od. 3.29 = Od. 7.37, Od. 2.413 = Od. 8.46 = 104, Od. 5.192, Od. 14.48. 3 To lead the way, give a lead, in a course of action. With dat.: τοῖσιν εὐπείθης ἡγήσατο νηπιέῃσιν (in their . . .) Od. 24.469. To give a lead, cause a start to be made. With dat. and genit. of that in which a start is made: ἀοιδὸς ἡμῖν ἡγείσθω ὀρχηθμοῖο Od. 23.134. 4 To be the leader, commander or chief of. a With genit.: ἐπικούρων Il. 12.101. Cf. Il. 2.567, 620, 638, 678, 731, 851, 867, 870. b With dat.: Μῄοσιν Il. 2.864, νῆες, ᾗσιν Ἀχιλλεὺς ἐς Τροίην ἡγεῖτο (brought to Troy under his command) Il. 16.169. Cf. Il. 2.687, Il. 5.211: Od. 14.238. 5 Absol., to act as chief or leader, lead one's men Il. 12.251 = Il. 13.833, Il. 13.802, Il. 14.374: Od. 14.470. To lead a person on, induce him to follow: κερδοσύνῃ ἡγήσατο Il. 22.247. 6 To lead or lead on (one's men). With genit.: ἡγήσατο λαῶν Il. 15.311. With dat.: Τρωσὶ ποτὶ πτόλιν ἡγήσασθαι Il. 22.101. 7 To take the lead, be the leading person, among. With dat.: ἡγεῖτο μνηστῆρσιν Od. 16.397.

ηγερεθομαι.g: [ἀγείρομαι. Cf. ἠερέθομαι beside ἀείρομαι.] 1 To come or gather together, assemble: ἀμφʼ Ἀτρεΐωνα ἠγερέθοντο Il. 23.233. Cf. Il. 2.304, Il. 10.127, Il. 19.303, Il. 24.783: περὶ ἑταῖροι ἠγερέθοντο Od. 2.392. Cf. Od. 3.412, Od. 11.228, Od. 17.34, 65, Od. 18.41, Od. 19.542, Od. 24.468. 2 To be or remain gathered together or in a body: ἀμφί μιν κρητῶν ἀγοὶ ἠγερέθονται Il. 3.231. Cf. Il. 12.82.

ηγηλαζω.g: [*ἡγηλός, apt to lead, fr. ἡγέομαι.] 1 To play the leader or fugleman to: κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει Od. 17.217. 2 To lead (a specified kind of existence), endure (a specified fate): κακὸν μόρον ἡγηλάζεις Od. 11.618.

ηγητωρ.g: -ορος, ὁ [ἡγέομαι.] A leader, commander or chief: δύω ἡγήτορες ἦσαν Il. 4.393. Cf. Il. 2.79, Il. 3.153, Il. 10.181, Il. 15.330, Il. 20.383, etc.: Ταφίων Od. 1.105. Cf. Od. 7.98, 136, 186 = Od. 8.26 = 97 = 387 = 536, Od. 8.11, Od. 11.526, Od. 13.186, 210. With ἀνήρ: Πυλίων ἡγήτορες ἄνδρες Il. 11.687. Cf. Il. 16.495, 532.

ηδε.g: [ἦ2δέ.] And: ταύρων ἠδʼ αἰγῶν Il. 1.41. Cf. Il. 1.96, 251, Il. 2.27, 79, 118, etc.: Od. 1.13, 95, 135, 170, 182, 231, etc. So ἠδὲ καί: Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 1.334, etc. Cf. Od. 2.209, etc. Correlative with ἠμέν. See ἠμέν.

ηδη.g: [ἦ2 δή.] 1 Previously to some specified or indicated time, by or before this (or that) time, by now, now, already, ere this: ἤδη οἱ ἐφῆκα βέλος Il. 5.188. Cf. Il. 1.250, 260, 590, Il. 2.699, Il. 3.56, 184, etc.: ἤδη Ἄϊδόσδε βεβήκει Od. 3.410. Cf. Od. 2.164, 211, 402, 410, Od. 3.241, 335, etc. Reinforcing νῦν Il. 15.110, etc.: Od. 14.213, etc. 2 In reference to the future, now: ἧ ἤδη με δαμόωσιν Il. 6.368. Cf. Il. 11.821, Il. 16.438, Il. 23.20, Il. 24.635, etc.: ἤδη σχεθέτω φόρμιγγα Od. 8.537. Cf. Od. 1.303, Od. 4.294, Od. 13.151, Od. 19.300, Od. 22.101, Od. 24.506, etc. Reinforcing νῦν Il. 1.456, etc.: Od. 10.472, etc.

ηδοσ.g: τό [cf. ἡδύς.] Pleasure, profit, satisfaction: μίνυνθα ἡμέων ἔσσεται ἠ. (we shall profit our friends little) Il. 11.318, τί μοι τῶν ἠ.; (what satisfaction have I in that ?) Il. 18.80. Cf. Il. 1.576: = Od. 18.404, Od. 24.95.

ηδυεπησ.g: [ἡδύς + ἔπος.] Sweet-speaking, silvertongued. Of Nestor Il. 1.248.

ηδυποτοσ.g: [ἡδύς + πο-, πίνω.] Sweet to drink. Of wine Od. 2.340, Od. 3.391, Od. 15.507.

ηδυσ.g: ἡδεῖα, ἡδύ. Also fem. ἡδύς Od. 12.369 [σϝαδ- as in ἁνδάνω.] 1 Sweet or pleasant. a To the taste. Of wine Od. 2.350, Od. 3.51, Od. 4.746, Od. 7.265, Od. 9.162, etc. Of a meal: δεῖπνον Od. 20.391. b To the sense of smell: ὀδμή Od. 9.210. Cf. Od. 12.369. c To the ear: ἀοιδήν Od. 8.64. 2 Of sleep or rest, sweet, grateful, balmy, refreshing Il. 4.131: Od. 1.364 = Od. 16.451 = Od. 19.604 = Od. 21.358, Od. 15.44, Od. 19.510, Od. 23.17. Superl. ἥδιστος: ὕπνος Od. 13.80. 3 Pleasing, agreeable, such as commends itself to one: εἴ πως τόδε πᾶσι φίλον καὶ ἡδὺ γένοιτο Il. 4.17. Cf. Il. 7.387: Od. 24.435. 4 In neut. ἡδύ as adv. a So as to gratify the sense of smell, sweetly: ἀμβροσίην ἡδὺ πνείουσαν Od. 4.446. b Of sleeping, sweetly: ἡδὺ κνώσσουσα Od. 4.809. c Of laughing, merrily, heartily: ἡδὺ γελάσσας Il. 11.378. Cf. Il. 2.270, Il. 21.508, Il. 23.784: = Od. 20.358 = Od. 21.376, Od. 16.354, Od. 18.35, 111.

ηε.g:
See ἠέ 2.
(ἠϝέ), ἤ. 1 Disjunctive particle. a Or: ἐγὼ ἢ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν Il. 2.231. Cf. Il. 1.40, 515, Il. 2.800, Il. 3.394, Il. 4.83, 142, etc.: εἰλαπίνη ἠὲ γάμος; Od. 1.226. Cf. Od. 1.162, 282, Od. 2.375, Od. 3.94, Od. 4.45, 396, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) Il. 19.148. b ἠὲ (ἢ) . . . ἠὲ (ἢ) . . ., either . . . or . . .: ἢ νῦν δηθύνοντʼ ἢ ὕστερον αὖτις ἰόντα Il. 1.27. Cf. Il. 1.138, 395, Il. 5.484, Il. 9.78, 537, Il. 10.370, etc.: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀμφαδόν Od. 1.296. Cf. Od. 3.99, 217, Od. 4.546, Od. 5.484, Od. 6.103, Od. 10.228, etc. Thrice or four times Il. 1.145, Il. 7.179, Il. 10.6, etc.: Od. 10.433, Od. 15.84, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) . . . ἤ τε (ἤτε) . . . Il. 9.276 = Il. 19.177, Il. 11.410, Il. 17.42.– ἢ . . . τε Il. 2.289. 2 In questions in disjunctive form (the second particle written ἦε, ἦ). a Direct: ἠέ τι βέβληαι, ἦε . . .; Il. 13.251. Cf. Il. 15.735, etc.: Od. 3.72, Od. 24.109, etc. Thrice Il. 13.308, etc. Without the particle in the first clause Il. 15.203, etc.: Od. 20.130, Od. 21.194, etc. b Indirect, whether . . . or . . .: μερμήριξεν, ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 1.190. Cf. Il. 2.238, Il. 4.15, Il. 5.86, Il. 8.377, Il. 13.327, Il. 18.308 (and see whether . . .), etc.: ὄφρʼ ἐῢ εἰδῶ, ἠὲ . . . ἦ . . . Od. 1.175. Cf. Od. 1.268, Od. 3.170, Od. 4.28, Od. 6.142, Od. 11.175, Od. 16.260, Od. 19.525, etc. Without the particle in the first clause Il. 10.546, etc.: Od. 4.837, etc. With εἰ or αἴ in the first clause Il. 2.368, Il. 6.368, Il. 8.533, Il. 22.246: Od. 24.218. With change of construction Od. 17.275. 3 After comparatives, than: ἀρείοσιν ἠέ περ ὑμῖν Il. 1.260. Cf. Il. 5.531, Il. 8.190, Il. 16.688, etc.: νεώτεροι ἢ πάρος ἦσαν Od. 10.395. Cf. Od. 1.322, Od. 8.154, etc. So ἤ τε (ἤτε) Od. 16.216. After ἄλλος Il. 10.404, etc. After ἀλλοῖος Od. 16.181, Od. 19.267. After verbs implying comparison: βούλομαι . . . ἢ . . . Il. 1.117, etc.: ἔφθης . . . ἢ . . . Od. 11.58, etc.
ᾔει 3 sing. impf. εἶμι.

ηελιοσ.g: -ου, ὁ. Also Ἥλιος Od. 8.271. Ἠέλιος as voc. Il. 3.277. 1 The sun. a ἅμʼ ἠελίῳ καταδύντι (at sunset) Il. 1.592, ἠ. ἐπέλαμψεν Il. 17.650. Cf. Il. 1.475, Il. 4.44, Il. 5.267, Il. 8.485, 538, Il. 10.547, Il. 14.185, etc.: Od. 2.181, Od. 4.45, Od. 6.98, Od. 7.124, Od. 10.160, Od. 15.404, Od. 20.356, etc. b ὑπʼ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο, in the upper world, among the living Od. 11.498, 619, Od. 15.349. Of seeing the sun, i.e. of living: δηρὸν ἔτʼ ὄψεσθαι φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 5.120. Cf. Il. 18.61 = 442, Il. 24.558: Od. 4.540 = Od. 10.498, Od. 4.833, Od. 14.44 = Od. 20.207. Sim. of being born: ἠελίου ἴδεν αὐγάς Il. 16.188. Of leaving the sun, i.e. of dying: λείψειν (λιπὼν) φάος ἠελίοιο Il. 18.11: Od. 11.93. 2 The quarter of the rising sun, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240. 3 The sun-god: Ἠ. ὃς πάντʼ ἐφορᾷς Il. 3.277. Cf. Il. 3.104, Il. 8.480, Il. 14.344, Il. 19.197, etc.: βοῦς Ὑπερίονος Ἠελίοιο Od. 1.8. Cf. Od. 3.1, Od. 8.271, Od. 10.138, Od. 11.16, 109, Od. 12.133, Od. 19.276, Od. 24.12, etc.

ηερεθομαι.g: [ἀείρομαι. Cf. ἠγερέθομαι beside ἀγείρομαι.] 1 To take wing: ὡς ἀκρίδες ἠερέθονται Il. 21.12. 2 To wave about, flutter: θύσανοι ἠερέθονται Il. 2.448. Fig., of the mind, to be blown about by passion or caprice, to be unsteady or untrustworthy Il. 3.108.

ηεριοσ.g: -η (ἠϝέριος) [ἀϝερ-. Cf. ἠώς, ἄριστον, αὔριον, ἦρι, λ. aurora.] With the early morning: ἠερίη ἀνέβη οὐρανόν Il. 1.497. Cf. Il. 1.557, Il. 3.7: Od. 9.52.

ηεροειδησ.g: -ές [ἠερ-, ἀήρ + εἶδος.] 1 Epithet of the sea, misty, melting into the haze of distance Il. 23.744: Od. 2.263, Od. 3.105, 294, Od. 4.482, Od. 5.164, 281, Od. 8.568 = Od. 13.150 = 176, Od. 12.285. In neut. ἠεροειδές as adv., through the haze, in the haze of distance: ὅσσον ἠ. ἀνὴρ ἴδεν Il. 5.770. 2 Of a rock, shrouded in mist Od. 12.233 (cf. 74). 3 Epithet of caves, dim, dusky, shadowy Od. 12.80, Od. 13.103 = 347, 366.

ηεροεισ.g: -εντος [ἠερ-, ἀήρ.] 1 Hazy, gloomy, dark: τάρταρον Il. 8.13, ζόφον Il. 12.240, Il. 15.191, Il. 21.56, Il. 23.51: Od. 11.57, 155, Od. 13.241. 2 Hazy, misty: κατʼ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα (through the paths of the clouds) Od. 20.64.

ηεροφοιτισ.g: [ἠερ-, ἀήρ + φοιτάω.] Walking in darkness. Epithet of Erinys Il. 9.571, Il. 19.87.

ηεροφωνοσ.g: [perh. fr. ἀείρω + φωνή. Cf. ἠερέθομαι, μετ-ήορος. Lifting up the voice.] Thus, loud-voiced. Epithet of heralds Il. 18.505.

ηθειοσ.g: -η. In voc. ἠθεῖε as a form of address to an elder or a master Il. 6.518 (Paris to Hector), Il. 10.37 (Menelaus to Agamemnon), Il. 22.229, 239 (the supposed Deïphobus to Hector). Sim. in the periphrasis ἠθείη κεφαλή Il. 23.94 (Achilles to the shade of Patroclus. Patroclus was the senior Il. 11.787). In Od. 14.147 (ἠθεῖόν μιν καλέω) Eumaeus means that he mentally addresses his absent master as ἠθεῖε.

ηθοσ.g: τό [conn. with ἔθω and orig. σϝῆθος.] In pl., the accustomed haunts of animals: ἤθεα ἵππων Il. 6.511 = Il. 15.268. The sties of swine Od. 14.411.

ηια1,.g: τά. Contr. ᾖα Od. 5.266, Od. 9.212. 1 Provisions for a voyage: ὅπλισσον ἤϊα Od. 2.289, ἤϊα φερώμεθα 410, ἤῗά κε πάντα κατέφθιτο Od. 4.363, ἐν καὶ ᾖα κωρύκῳ Od. 5.266, Od. 9.212, νηὸς ἐξέφθιτο ἤῗα πάντα Od. 12.329. 2 Prey: θώων ἤϊα πέλονται Il. 13.103. 3 Chaff (in this sense perh. a different word): ὡς ἄνεμος ζαὴς ἠΐων (disyllable) θημῶνα τινάξῃ Od. 5.368.

ηιοεισ.g: -εντος. Epithet of a river, of unknown meaning: ἐπʼ ἠϊόεντι σκαμάνδρῳ Il. 5.36.

ηιοσ.g: Epithet of Apollo, of unknown meaning: ἤϊε Φοῖβε Il. 15.365, Il. 20.152.

ηιων.g: -όνος, ἡ. Dat. pl. ἠϊόνεσσι Od. 5.156. 1 A beach or shore of the sea: ἠϊόνος προπάροιθε βαθείης Il. 2.92. Cf. Il. 7.462, Il. 12.31, Il. 14.36, Il. 20.148, Il. 23.61. 2 In pl. a Portions of the shore, beaches, shores: ἀμφʼ ἄκραι ἠϊόνες βοόωσιν (to their furthest points) Il. 17.265 (v.l. ἄκραι ἠϊόνος, taking ἄκραι as sb. (see ἄκρη 3) and ἠϊόνος in sense (1), the headlands of the shore), ἠὼς φαινομένη ὑπεὶρ ἅλα τʼ ἠϊόνας τε Il. 24.13. Cf. Od. 5.156. b Beaches or spits projecting into the sea: ἠϊόνας παραπλῆγας Od. 5.418 = 440. Cf. Od. 6.138.

ηκα.g:
1 Of action, gently, without effort: ψύξασα Il. 20.440. Cf. Il. 23.336: Od. 18.92, 94, Od. 20.301. Gently, without violence: ἀπώσατο γέροντα Il. 24.508. 2 Of journeying, softly, at a foot-pace Od. 17.254. 3 Of speaking, softly, in an undertone Il. 3.155. 4 Of the soft play of light on a glossy surface: χιτῶνας ἦκα στίλβοντας ἐλαίῳ Il. 18.596.
aor. ἵημι1.

ηκεστοσ.g: -η [doubtfully explained as fr. ἠ- = ἀ-1 + -κεστος. See κεστός.] Thus, untouched by the goad: βοῦς ἠκέστας Il. 6.94 = 275, 309.

ηκιστοσ.g: [superl. fr. ἦκα. Cf. ἥσσων.] The slowest or weakest: ἠ. ἐλαυνέμεν (in driving) Il. 23.531.

ηλακατα.g: τά [ἠλακάτη.] The yarn spun off from the distaff Od. 6.53, 306, Od. 7.105, Od. 17.97, Od. 18.315.

ηλασκαζω.g: [cf. ἠλάσκω.] 1 To wander aimlessly about Il. 18.281. 2 To go about or skulk in order to avoid (danger): ὅππῃ ἐμὸν μένος ἠλασκάζει Od. 9.457.

ηλασκω.g: [ἄλη.] To rove or flit about: ἔλαφοι καθʼ ὕλην αὔτως ἠλάσκουσαι Il. 13.104. Cf. Il. 2.470.

ηλεκτρον.g: τό. 1 Amber Od. 4.73. 2 In pl., beads of amber: ὅρμον ἠλέκτροισιν ἐερμένον Od. 18.296. Cf. Od. 15.460.

ηλεοσ.g: [app. conn. with ἀλάομαι, ἠλάσκω.] Voc. ἠλέ Il. 15.128. 1 Crazed, distraught: φρένας ἠλέ (in your . . .) Il. 15.128. Cf. Od. 2.243. 2 That takes away one's wits or discretion: οἶνος Od. 14.464.

ηλιβατοσ.g: -ον. Of unknown meaning. Epithet of πέτρη Il. 15.273, 619, Il. 16.35: Od. 9.243, Od. 10.88, Od. 13.196.

ηλιθα.g: [poss. conn. with ἅλις.] Strengthening πολλός: ἤλιθα πολλήν Il. 11.677. Cf. Od. 5.483, Od. 9.330, Od. 14.215, Od. 19.443.

ηλικιη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἧλιξ.] 1 Time of life: ἤν πως ἡλικίην αἰδέσσεται (may respect my age) Il. 22.419. 2 Those of the same age as oneself, one's fellows in years, one's contemporaries: ἡλικίην ἐκέκαστο Il. 16.808.

ηλιξ.g: -ικος. Of the same age: βόες Od. 18.373.

ηλιτομηνοσ.g: [ἀλιτ-, ἀλιταίνω + μήν. Failing in (the due number of) months.] Untimely born Il. 19.118.

ηλοσ.g: -ου, ὁ [ϝῆλος. Cf. L. vallus.] A nail or stud used for ornament Il. 1.246, Il. 11.29, 633.

ηλυσιοσ.g: [said to be for ἠλύθ-τιος, fr. ἠλυθ- (see ἔρχομαι). To which . . . go.] Ἠλύσιον πεδίον, an abode of everlasting bliss assigned to mortals favoured by the gods Od. 4.563.

ημα.g: -ατος, τό [ἡ-, ἵημι1.] A throwing or hurling. In pl.: ὅσσον ἥμασιν ἔπλευ ἄριστος (in throwing the spear) Il. 23.891.

ημαθοεισ.g: -εντος [ἄμαθος.] Abounding in sand, sandy, by the sandy shore. Epithet of Pylus Il. 2.77, Il. 9.153 = 295, Il. 11.712: Od. 1.93, Od. 2.214 = 359, Od. 2.326, Od. 4.633, Od. 11.257, 459, Od. 24.152.

ημαρ.g: -ατος, τό [cf. ἡμέρη.] 1 Day, the day, the period of daylight: μέσον ἠ. Il. 21.111, ὄφρʼ ἀέξετο ἠ. Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84: = Od. 9.56. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 10.86, 470, Od. 17.191, Od. 18.367 = Od. 22.301. For δείελον ἠ. see δείελος 2. 2 A day considered as a space of time. a As a period of daylight: πᾶν ἠ. Il. 1.592, νύκτας τε καὶ ἠ. Il. 5.490. Cf. Il. 1.601, Il. 9.326, Il. 18.340, 453, Il. 19.162, Il. 22.432, Il. 23.186, Il. 24.73, 713, 745: Od. 2.345, Od. 5.156, 388, Od. 9.74, 161 = 556 = Od. 10.183 = 476 = Od. 12.29 = Od. 19.424, Od. 10.11, 28, 80 = Od. 15.476, Od. 10.142, Od. 11.183 = Od. 13.338 = Od. 16.39, Od. 16.365, Od. 17.515, Od. 19.513, Od. 20.84, Od. 24.41, 63. b As embracing both daylight and dark: ἐείκοσιν ἤματα Il. 6.217, ἤματα πάντα Il. 8.539 (for ever), Il. 12.133 (ever), Il. 13.826, Il. 14.235 (all my days), 269, 276, Il. 16.499, Il. 23.594, Il. 24.491: Od. 2.205, Od. 4.209, 592, Od. 5.136 = Od. 7.257 = Od. 23.336, Od. 5.210, 219, Od. 6.46, 281, Od. 7.94, Od. 8.431, Od. 9.123, Od. 10.467, Od. 15.54, Od. 21.156, Od. 23.6, Od. 24.25. Cf. Il. 21.45: Od. 4.360, Od. 5.278, Od. 7.267, Od. 19.199. 3 A day considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series: ἤματι κείνῳ (on that day, that day) Il. 2.37, 482, Il. 4.543, Il. 18.324, Il. 21.517, τρίτῳ ἤματι Il. 11.707, ἤματα πάντα (during or on each day, every day) Il. 19.226. Cf. Il. 2.351, 743, Il. 3.189, Il. 4.164 = Il. 6.448, Il. 5.210, Il. 6.345, 422, Il. 8.475, Il. 9.253 = 439 = Il. 11.766, Il. 9.363, Il. 11.444, Il. 12.279, Il. 13.98, 335, Il. 14.250, Il. 15.76, 252, 719, Il. 16.385, Il. 17.401, Il. 18.85, Il. 19.60, 89, 98, Il. 21.5, 77, 584, Il. 22.359, 471, Il. 23.87: Od. 2.55 = Od. 17.534, Od. 3.180, Od. 5.34, 262, 309, 390 = Od. 9.76 = Od. 10.144, Od. 6.170, Od. 7.326, Od. 8.468, Od. 12.399 = Od. 15.477, Od. 18.137, Od. 19.153 = Od. 24.143, Od. 20.19, 116, Od. 23.252.– ἐπʼ ἤματι Il. 10.48 (in a single day), Il. 19.229 (for the day (and no longer)): Od. 2.284 (in one day), Od. 12.105 (in the day, a day), Od. 14.105 (each day, day by day). Cf. Il. 13.234, Il. 19.110. 4 With an adj., expressing periphrastically the substantival notion implicit in the adj. a αἴσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, the fate, one's fate) Il. 8.72, Il. 21.100, Il. 22.212: Od. 16.280. b ἠ. ἀναγκαῖον (the day that brings compulsion, slavery) Il. 16.836. c δούλιον ἠ. (the day that brings slavery, slavery) Il. 6.463: Od. 14.340, Od. 17.323. d ἐλεύθερον ἠ. (the day or time of freedom, freedom) Il. 6.455, Il. 16.831, Il. 20.193. e κακὸν ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 9.251, 597, Il. 20.315 = Il. 21.374: Od. 10.269, 288, Od. 15.524. f μόρσιμον ἠ. (the fatal day, one's fate) Il. 15.613: Od. 10.175.– g νηλεὲς ἠ. (the day of pitiless fate, fate, bane) Il. 11.484, 588, Il. 13.514, Il. 15.375, Il. 17.511, 615, Il. 21.57: Od. 8.525, Od. 9.17. h νόστιμον ἠ. (the day that brings one's home-coming, one's home-coming) Od. 1.9, 168, 354, Od. 3.233 = Od. 5.220 = Od. 8.466, Od. 6.311, Od. 16.149, Od. 17.253, 571, Od. 19.369. i ὀλέθριον ἠ. (the day that brings bane, bane) Il. 19.294, 409. j ἠ. ὀρφανικόν (the day that brings orphanhood, orphanhood) Il. 22.490.

ηματιοσ.g: -η [ἠματ-, ἦμαρ.] 1 By day, in the day-time: ἠματίη ὑφαίνεσκεν Od. 2.104 = Od. 24.139. Cf. Od. 19.149. 2 Day by day, daily Il. 9.72.

ημεν.g:
1 pl. impf. εἰμί.
[ἦ2 μέν.] Correlative with ἠδέ. ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . ., both . . . and . . .: ἠμὲν νέοι ἠδὲ γέροντες Il. 2.789. Cf. Il. 5.751, Il. 9.36, Il. 11.7, Il. 12.159, Il. 15.226, etc.: ἠμὲν ἀπείλησας . . . ἠδὲ . . . (you boasted that . . . and lo . . .) Od. 8.383. Cf. Od. 1.97, Od. 2.68, Od. 3.105, Od. 10.22, Od. 14.193, etc. So ἠμὲν . . . ἠδὲ . . . ἠδὲ . . . Il. 4.258, etc.– ἠμὲν . . . δὲ . . . Il. 12.428.– ἠμὲν . . . τε . . . Od. 8.575. Retaining something of the original emphasis (surely . . . and even so . . .) Il. 1.453, etc.

ημερισ.g: ἡ [ἥμερος. Cf. κραταιός, κραταιΐς.] The cultivated vine, the vine Od. 5.69.

ημετερονδε.g: [acc. of ἡμέτερος + -δε 1.] To our (my) house: ἡ. ἐλθόντες Od. 8.39. Cf. Od. 15.513, Od. 24.267.

ημετεροσ.g: -η, -ον [ἡμεῖς.] 1 Our Il. 2.374, Il. 3.233, Il. 6.58, Il. 10.342, Il. 11.720, etc.: Od. 1.45, Od. 2.26, Od. 6.191, Od. 11.33, Od. 13.181, etc. With the article: αἱ ἡμέτεραι ἄλοχοι Il. 2.136. Absol.: εἰς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 2.55 = Od. 17.534.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (to our homes, home) Il. 9.619. 2 My Il. 1.30, Il. 6.151 = Il. 20.214, Il. 7.363, Il. 9.108, Il. 15.224, Il. 16.244, Il. 19.73, Il. 21.60, Il. 24.567: Od. 1.397, Od. 3.186, Od. 4.101, Od. 8.255, Od. 10.334, Od. 11.562, Od. 16.45, 117, 300, 442, Od. 19.344, Od. 21.375, Od. 22.464, Od. 24.216. Absol.: ἐς ἡμέτερον (sc. δῶμα) Od. 7.301.–ἐφʼ ἡμέτερα (sc. δώματα) (home) Od. 15.88. (Sometimes, esp. in uses with οἶκος and the like, it is difficult to say which sense should be preferred.)

ημιθεοσ.g: [ἡμι- + θεός.] Half-divine, of divine parentage on one side: ἀνδρῶν Il. 12.23.

ημιονειοσ.g: -η, -ον [ἡμίονος.] 1 Drawn by mules Il. 24.189, 266: Od. 6.72. 2 For, worn by, mules Il. 24.268.

ημιονοσ.g: -ου, ὁ, ἡ [ἡμι- + ὄνος. A half-ass.] 1 A mule (doubtless including the hinny) Il. 7.333, Il. 10.352, Il. 17.742, Il. 23.121, Il. 24.150, etc.: Od. 4.636, Od. 6.37, Od. 7.2, Od. 8.124, Od. 15.85, Od. 17.298, etc. In Il. 2.852 (ἡμιόνων ἀγροτεράων) app. not strictly mules but some species intermediate between the horse and the ass. 2 Like ἵππος 3: ἐφʼ ἡμιόνων κείμενον (i.e. on the waggon) Il. 24.702.

ημιπελεκκον.g: -ου, τό [ἡμι- + πέλεκκον in sense axe.] A half-axe, an axe with a single cutting edge Il. 23.851, 858, 883.

ημισυσ.g: -υ [ἡμι-.] 1 Half, half of: ἡμίσεες λαοί Od. 3.155. 2 Absol., half of what is specified or indicated. a ἡμίσεες εἰλεῦντο Il. 21.7. Cf. Od. 3.157, Od. 24.464. b In neut. ἥμισυ: τιμῆς ἡ. Il. 6.193. Cf. Il. 9.580 (following τὸ ἡ. 579 (see below)), Il. 17.231 (twice): Od. 9.246 (twice), Od. 13.114, Od. 17.322. With the article: τὸ δʼ ἡ. κεῖτʼ ἐπὶ γαίης Il. 13.565. Cf. Il. 9.579 3 In neut. as adv., to the extent of a half: ἡ. μείρεο τιμῆς Il. 9.616.

ημιταλαντον.g: τό [ἡμι- + τάλαντον.] A halftalent: χρυσοῦ Il. 23.751, 796.

ημοσ.g: When, at the time when. 1 With indic.: ἦμος δʼ ἠέλιος κατέδυ Il. 1.475. Cf. Il. 1.477, Il. 16.779, etc.: Od. 2.1, Od. 9.58, 168, etc. Introducing a simile Od. 12.439. Correlative with τῆμος. See τῆμος 2. 2 With subj. in a conditional relative sentence. See Table at end III.B.a 1.

ημυω.g: (ὑπεμνήμυκε.) 1 To cause to bend, bow, droop: κάρη Il. 8.308. 2 To bend, bow, droop: λήϊον ἠμύει ἀσταχύεσσιν (with its ears) Il. 2.148, ἤμυσε καρήατι Il. 19.405. Of a city nodding or tottering to its fall Il. 2.373 = Il. 4.290.

ημων.g:
-ονος, ὁ [ἡ-, ἵημι1.] One skilled in throwing (the spear): ἥμονες ἄνδρες Il. 23.886.
3 pl. impf. ἀμάω1.

ην.g:
3 sing. impf. εἰμί.
[εἰ ἄν.] With subj. 1 Introducing in protasis one of two opposed clauses, even if, even though, though, granted that = εἰ 4. For the examples see (II) of Table at end. 2 Introducing the protasis of conditional sentences, if, on condition that, supposing that = εἰ 5. For the examples see (III) of Table. 3 In final clauses, if haply, in the hope that = εἰ 9..b: ἐμὲ πρόες, ἤν πού τι φόως Δαναοῖσι γένωμαι Il. 16.39. Cf. Il. 7.39, Il. 14.78, Il. 17.245, Il. 20.172, Il. 22.419: ἤν που ἀκούσῃ (ἀκούσω) Od. 1.94, Od. 2.360, Od. 3.83. Cf. Od. 1.282, Od. 2.216, Od. 5.417. 4 In an object clause, whether = εἰ 10 b : ὄφρα ἴδῃ ἤν τοι χραίσμῃ φιλότης Il. 15.32.

ηνεμοεισ.g: -εσσα [ἄνεμος.] Blown upon or vexed by the winds: ἄκριας Od. 9.400, Od. 16.365. Cf. Il. 22.145: Od. 19.432. Epithet of places. Of Troy Il. 3.305, Il. 8.499 = Il. 12.115, Il. 13.724, Il. 18.174, Il. 23.64, 297. Of Enispe Il. 2.606. Of Mimas Od. 3.172.

ηνια.g: τά. The reins used in driving a chariot Il. 3.261, Il. 5.226, 262, 365, Il. 8.121, Il. 16.404, Il. 17.619, Il. 23.337, etc.: Od. 3.483, Od. 6.81.

ηνιοχευσ.g: ὁ. 1 = ἡνίοχος 1 Il. 5.505, Il. 8.312, Il. 16.737. 2 Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνίοχος 2) Il. 19.401.

ηνιοχευω.g: [ἡνίοχος.] 1 To act as ἡνίοχος of a war-chariot, drive it Il. 11.103, Il. 23.641, 642. 2 To drive a waggon Od. 6.319.

ηνιοχοσ.g: -ου, ὁ [ἡνία + ὀχ-, ἔχω. He that holds the reins.] 1 The driver of a war-chariot as distinguished from the παραιβάτης or fighting man: παραιβάται ἡνίοχοί τε Il. 23.132. Cf. Il. 5.231, 580, Il. 8.119, 124 = 316, Il. 8.126, Il. 11.47 = Il. 12.84, Il. 11.161, 273 = 399, Il. 11.280, Il. 12.111, Il. 13.386, 394, 537 = Il. 14.431, Il. 17.427, 439, 610, Il. 18.225, Il. 23.280. 2 Used loosely of the παραιβάτης (cf. ἡνιοχεύς 2): θρασὺν ἡνίοχον φορέοντες Ἕκτορα Il. 8.89 (Eniopeus was driving, see 119, where he also is called ἡ.). In pl. including both the ἡ. proper and the παραιβάτης: σὺν ἡνιόχοισι κακοῖσιν Il. 17.487. 3 One who drives his chariot in a race: μήτι ἡ. περιγίγνεται ἡνιόχοιο Il. 23.318. Cf. Il. 23.460, 465, 502.

ηνισ.g: [doubtfully explained as fr. ἔνος, cited in sense year.] Thus, one year old, that is a yearling: δυοκαίδεκα βοῦς ἤνις Il. 6.94 = 275, 309, βοῦν ἦνιν Il. 10.292: = Od. 3.382.

ηνορεη.g: -ης, ἡ [ἀνήρ.] Instrumental ἠνορέηφι Il. 4.303. Manliness, valour, mettle, prowess: ἠνορέηφι πεποιθώς Il. 4.303. Cf. Il. 6.156, Il. 8.226 = Il. 11.9, Il. 17.329: Od. 24.509.

ηνοψ.g: -οπος. Of unknown meaning. Perh. glittering, gleaming, or the like: ἤνοπι χαλκῷ Il. 16.408, Il. 18.349: = Od. 10.360.

ηοιοσ.g: -η, -ον [ἠώς.] 1 Of the east, dwelling in the east, eastern Od. 8.29. 2 In fem. as sb., the morning: πᾶσαν ἠοίην μένομεν Od. 4.447.

ηοσ.g: Also ἕως Od. 2.78. This form scanned as a monosyllable Il. 17.727. 1 While, so long as: ἧος ζώει Od. 17.390. Cf. Od. 19.530. Correlative with τόφρα. See τόφρα 3. 2 While, during the time that: ἧος ὁ ταῦθʼ ὥρμαινεν Il. 1.193: = Od. 4.120 = Od. 5.365, ἧός μοι πάρʼ ὀϊστοί (while I still have them) Od. 22.106. Cf. Od. 13.315 = Od. 15.153, Od. 17.358. Correlative with τόφρα. See τόφρα 3. With τῆος. See τῆος 2. 3 For a time, up to a certain point of time: ἕως μὲν θέουσιν Il. 17.727. Cf. Il. 12.141, Il. 13.143, Il. 15.277, Il. 17.730: Od. 2.148, Od. 3.126 (all that time). 4 Until. a With indic.: ἧος ὤλεσε θυμόν Il. 11.342 = Il. 20.412. Cf. Il. 11.488: Od. 5.429, Od. 7.280, Od. 9.233, Od. 13.321, Od. 15.109. b With subj. α Pure: ἧος ἵκηται ἰσόπεδον Il. 13.141. β With κεν: ἧός κε τέλος κιχείω Il. 3.291. Cf. Il. 17.622, Il. 24.154, 183. c With opt. α Pure: ἧος θερμαίνοιτο (to remain there till it should . . .) Od. 9.376. Cf. Od. 23.151. β With κεν: ἕως κʼ ἀπὸ πάντα δοθείη Od. 2.78. Correlative with τόφρα. See τόφρα 3. 5 In order that. With opt.: ἦος χυτλώσαιτο Od. 6.80. Cf. Od. 4.800, Od. 5.386. After a vb. of praying, that. With opt.: ἀρώμενος ἧος ἵκοιο γῆρας Od. 19.367.

ηπεδανοσ.g: [prob. for ἀ-πεδ-ανός fr. ἀ-1 + πεδ-, ποδ-, πούς. Not firm on the feet. Cf. ἔμπεδος.] Thus, weakly, feeble Il. 8.104: Od. 8.311.

ηπειρονδε.g: [acc. of ἤπειρος. + -δε 1.] 1 To or on to the land as opposed to the sea: ἐκ πόντου βὰς ἠ. Od. 5.56. Cf. Od. 5.438, Od. 9.73, 485, Od. 10.403, 423, Od. 13.116, Od. 23.236. 2 To the mainland as opposed to an island: πέμψω σʼ ἠ. Od. 18.84, ἀνάξομέν μιν ἠ. 115 (in both cases said in Ithaca).

ηπειροσ.g: -ου, ἡ. 1 The land as opposed to the sea: νῆʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείροιο ἔρυσσαν Il. 1.485: εἴτʼ ἐπʼ ἠπείρου . . . εἴτʼ ἐν πελάγει Od. 3.90. Cf. Od. 1.162, Od. 5.348, 350, 399, 402, Od. 9.85 = Od. 10.56, Od. 9.496, Od. 13.114, Od. 14.136, Od. 16.325, 359, 367. 2 Inland parts as opposed to the coast Od. 9.49. 3 The mainland, as opposed to an island or islands: οἳ ἤπειρον ἕχον Il. 2.635 (the coast of the mainland opposite the islands): οὔτʼ ἠπείροιο οὔτʼ αὐτῆς Ἰθάκης Od. 14.97. Cf. Od. 13.235, Od. 14.100, Od. 21.109, Od. 24.378.

ηπεροπευσ.g: ὁ [ἠπεροπεύω.] A cheat, deceiver, cozener, beguiler: ἠπεροπῆά τε καὶ ἐπίκλοπον Od. 11.364.

ηπεροπευω.g: 1 To deceive, cozen: ἵνʼ ἐμὰς φρένας ἠπεροπεύσῃς Od. 13.327. Absol. Od. 14.400. To trick, take unfair advantage of Il. 23.605. 2 To beguile the heart of, lead astray (a woman) Il. 5.349: Od. 15.419. So τάτε φρένας ἠπεροπεύει γυναιξίν Od. 15.421. With direct and cognate acc.: τί με ταῦτα λιλαίεαι ἠπεροπεύειν; (to beguile me thus) Il. 3.399.

ηπιοδωροσ.g: -ον [ἤπιος + δῶρον.] App., generous in giving, bountiful in supplying her children's needs, grudging them nothing: μήτηρ Il. 6.251.

ηπιοσ.g: -η, -ον. 1 Well or kindly disposed, kindly, gentle, mild, not harsh or rigorous: ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν (is well disposed towards me) Il. 4.361 (see εἴδω III.12), ἐθέλω τοι ἠ. εἶναι Il. 8.40 = Il. 22.184. Cf. Il. 24.770, 775: Od. 2.47, 230 = Od. 5.8, Od. 2.234 = Od. 5.12, Od. 10.337, Od. 11.441, Od. 13.314, Od. 14.139, Od. 15.152, 490. Absol. in neut. pl.: εἴ μοι ἤπια εἰδείη (were well disposed towards me) Il. 16.73: ὁμῶς τοι ἤπια οἶδεν (is at one with you in loyalty of heart) Od. 13.405 = Od. 15.39, ἀνάκτεσιν ἤπια εἰδώς (loyal to them) Od. 15.557. See in reference to these εἴδω III.12. 2 Giving kindly tendance, solicitous for the well-being of what is committed to one Il. 23.281. 3 Of speech, tending to effect reconcilement or bring peace Od. 20.327. 4 Of medicinal applications, soothing, allaying pain Il. 4.218, Il. 11.515, 830.

ηπυτα.g: (ᾰ) [ἠπύω. Prob. orig. a voc. turned into a nom.]. Loud-voiced: κῆρυξ Il. 7.384.

ηπυω.g: (ἐπ-.) 1 To call to (a person): κύκλωπας Od. 9.399. Cf. Od. 10.83. 2 Of the wind, to roar Il. 14.399. Of the lyre, to sound Od. 17.271.

ηρ.g: (ϝήρ) [referred to var, to choose, wish.] What is pleasing or agreeable. Only in acc. sing. ἧρα in phrase ἦρα φέρειν, to do acceptable service, make oneself agreeable, show oneself well disposed: μητρὶ φίλῃ ἐπὶ ἦρα φέρων Il. 1.572. Cf. Il. 1.578: Od. 3.164, Od. 16.375, Od. 18.56. Sim.: θυμῷ ἦρα φέροντες (yielding to it, giving in to it) Il. 14.132.

ηρατο.g:
3 sing. contr. aor. mid. ἀείρω.
3 sing. impf. ἀράομαι.

ηρι.g: [ἀϝερ-. See ἠέριος.] Early in the morning Il. 9.360: Od. 19.320, Od. 20.156.

ηριον.g: τό. A grave-mound, a barrow Il. 23.126.

ηρωσ.g: -ωος. Genit. ἥρως Od. 6.303. Dat. ἥρωϊ Il. 9.613, Il. 13.582, Il. 17.137, Il. 23.151, etc.: Od. 2.99, Od. 19.144, Od. 24.134. ἥρῳ Il. 7.453: Od. 8.483. 1 A warrior: στίχας ἡρώων Il. 20.326. Cf. Il. 1.4, Il. 2.483, 579, Il. 16.144 = Il. 19.391, Il. 18.56 = 437, Il. 23.645: Od. 11.329, Od. 21.299. With ἄνδρες: στίχας ἀνδρῶν ἡρώων Il. 5.747 = Il. 8.391. Cf. Il. 9.525, Il. 13.346: Od. 1.101, Od. 4.268, Od. 11.629, Od. 24.25, 88. 2 Prefixed to an ethnic name, of a body of the same race in arms together: ὦ φίλοι ἥρωες Δαναοί Il. 2.110 = Il. 6.67 = Il. 15.733 = Il. 19.78. Cf. Il. 2.256, Il. 12.165, Il. 13.629, Il. 15.219, 230, 261, 702, Il. 19.34, 41: Od. 24.68. 3 Prefixed or added as a sort of title to the name or patronymic of a warrior: ἡ. Ἀτρεΐδης Il. 1.102 = Il. 7.322 = Il. 13.112, Λήϊτος ἡ. Il. 7.35. Cf. Il. 2.708, 844, Il. 4.200, Il. 6.63, Il. 7.453, Il. 9.613, Il. 11.339, 771, Il. 12.95, Il. 13.92, 384, 428, 439, 575, 582, Il. 16.751, 781, Il. 17.137, 706, Il. 18.325, Il. 21.163, Il. 22.298, Il. 23.151, 747, 893, Il. 24.474, 574: Od. 11.520. 4 In voc. as a form of address to a warrior Il. 10.416, Il. 20.104. With a proper name: Εὐρύπυλʼ ἥρως Il. 11.819, 838. 5 Applied to warriors, but signifying little more than the man, the wight: ἔτρεψεν ἀδελφειοῦ φρένας ἡ. Il. 6.61. Cf. Il. 3.377, Il. 7.120 = Il. 13.788, Il. 10.179, Il. 23.824. In apposition: ὅ γʼ ἡ. ἔστη Il. 5.308. Cf. Il. 5.327, Il. 8.268, Il. 10.154, Il. 11.483, Il. 13.164, Il. 23.896. 6 As an honourable appellation of others than warriors: ἐπὶ φᾶρος βάλετʼ ὤμοις ἡ. Od. 15.62. Cf. Od. 7.44, Od. 8.242. With ἄνδρες Od. 14.97. With an ethnic name: ἥρωας Ἀχαιούς Od. 1.272. 7 Prefixed or added as a sort of title to the name or patronymic of another than a warrior: Λαέρτην ἥρωα Od. 1.189. Cf. Od. 2.15, 99 = Od. 19.144 = Od. 24.134, Od. 2.157 = Od. 24.451, Od. 3.415, Od. 4.21 = 303, 617 = Od. 15.117, Od. 6.303, Od. 7.155, Od. 8.483, Od. 11.342, Od. 14.317, Od. 15.52, 121, 131, Od. 18.423, Od. 22.185. 8 In voc. as a form of address to another than a warrior Od. 4.423, Od. 7.303, Od. 10.516. With a proper name: Τηλέμαχʼ ἥρως Od. 4.312.

3 sing. aor. subj. ἵημι1.
3 sing. subj. εἰμί.

ησσων.g: -ονος [for ἡκιων. Comp. fr. ἦκα. Cf. ἤκιστος.] 1 Of less worth or merit, inferior Il. 16.722, Il. 23.322, 858. 2 In neut. ἧσσον as adv., less: ὀλίγον τί μʼ ἡ. ἐτίμα Od. 15.365.

ησυχιη.g: ἡ [ἡσύχιος.] Peace, freedom from disturbance: ἡ. ἂν ἐμοὶ καὶ μᾶλλον ἔτʼ εἴη Od. 18.22.

ητορ.g: τό. Only in nom. and acc. sing. 1 The heart: πάλλεται ἠ. ἀνὰ στόμα Il. 22.452. Cf. Il. 10.93. 2 The heart, breast, soul, mind. As the seat or a seat a α Of life, vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. θυμός I 1.a): εἰ χάλκεόν μοι ἠ. ἐνείη Il. 2.490: τετιημένος ἠ. Od. 7.287. Cf. Od. 4.703 = Od. 23.205, Od. 19.136, Od. 24.345. Hence β The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. θυμός I.1.b): μὴ ἠ. ὀλέσσῃς Il. 5.250. Cf. Il. 11.115 (of fawns), Il. 15.252, Il. 16.660, Il. 17.535, Il. 21.201, Il. 24.50: ἀπορραῖσαι ἠ. Od. 16.428. b Of spirit, courage, stoutness, resolution, endurance: ἄλκιμον ἠ. Il. 5.529. Cf. Il. 3.31, Il. 16.209, 242, 264 (of wasps), Il. 17.111 (of a lion), Il. 19.169, Il. 20.169 (of a lion), Il. 21.114, 425, 571, Il. 24.205, 521: μινύθει τοι ἠ. ἐταίρων Od. 4.374. Cf. Od. 4.467, 481 = Od. 10.496, Od. 5.297 = 406 = Od. 22.147, Od. 9.256, Od. 10.198 = 566 = Od. 12.277, Od. 22.68. c Of anger, wrath, passion: κεχολωμένος ἠ. (in his heart) Il. 14.367. Cf. Il. 10.107, Il. 24.585. d Of desire or appetite: σίτοιο ἄσασθαι ἠ. Il. 19.307. e Of volition: τίς σφῶϊν μαίνεται ἠ.; Il. 8.413. Cf. Il. 15.166, 182: δῶρον ὅττι κέ μοι δοῦναι ἠ. ἀνώγῃ Od. 1.316. f Of feelings, emotions, moods: τετιημέναι ἠ. Il. 8.437, χαίρει μοι ἠ. Il. 23.647. Cf. Il. 5.364, 670, Il. 9.9, 705, Il. 10.575 (their tired hearts), Il. 11.556, Il. 13.84, Il. 15.554, Il. 16.450, 509, Il. 19.366, Il. 21.389, Il. 22.169: ἠ. οἱ ἰάνθη Od. 4.840, τάφος οἱ ἠ. ἵκανεν Od. 23.93. Cf. Od. 1.48, 60, 114, Od. 2.298, Od. 4.538, 804, Od. 7.269, Od. 8.303, Od. 9.62 = 105 = 565 = Od. 10.77 = 133, Od. 10.313, Od. 13.286, 320, Od. 15.481, Od. 16.92, Od. 17.46, 514, Od. 18.153, Od. 20.22, 84, Od. 23.53. g Of the faculty of deliberating or considering: ἠ οἱ μερμήριξεν Il. 1.188. Of recollection: ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ἠ. Od. 19.224.– h Of one's character or dispostion: ἀμείλιχον ἠ. ἔχουσα Il. 9.572. Cf. Il. 9.497: Od. 23.172.

ηυγενειοσ.g: [ἠϋ-, εὐ- 5 + γενειάς.] Well-bearded. Epithet of lions Il. 15.275, Il. 17.109, Il. 18.318: Od. 4.456.

ηυκομοσ.g: -ον [ἠϋ-, εὐ- 5 + κόμη.] With beautiful hair, fair-tressed. Epithet of goddesses and women. Of Leto Il. 1.36, Il. 19.413: Od. 11.318. Of Thetis Il. 4.512, Il. 16.860. Of Athene Il. 6.92, 273, 303. Of Here Il. 10.5. Of Calypso Od. 8.452, Od. 12.389. Of Briseïs Il. 2.689. Of Helen Il. 3.329 = Il. 7.355 = Il. 8.82, Il. 9.339, Il. 11.369, 505, Il. 13.766. Of Niobe Il. 24.602.– μητέρος Il. 24.466.

ηυτε.g: [cf. εὖτε.] 1 As when, introducing similes. With indic. Il. 2.87, 455, 480, Il. 3.3, Il. 16.487, Il. 21.573, Il. 22.139. With subj. Il. 17.547. Without expressed vb. Il. 2.469, Il. 15.618, Il. 17.737: Od. 21.48. 2 Like, as: ἠΰτʼ ὀμίχλη Il. 1.359. Cf. Il. 2.754, Il. 4.243, Il. 7.219, Il. 19.374, etc.: Od. 8.280, 518, Od. 11.222, Od. 17.463, etc. 3 After a comp., than: μελάντερον ἠΰτε πίσσα Il. 4.277.

ηφαιστοσ.g: [use of the proper name.] A fire: σπλάγχνʼ ὑπείρεχον Ἡφαίστοιο Il. 2.426.

ηχηεισ.g: -εσσα (ϝηχήεις) [(ϝ)ηχή.] Sounding. Epithet of the sea Il. 1.157. Of a house, echoing Od. 4.72.

ηχι.g: [ᾗ (see ὅς2 II.6) + advbl. suff. -χι.] Where: ἡ. ἑκάστῳ δῶμα Ἥφαιστος ποίησεν Il. 1.607. Cf. Il. 3.326, Il. 5.774, Il. 8.14, Il. 11.76: Od. 3.292, Od. 6.94, Od. 19.553. In an object clause: ἄλλους πευθόμεθʼ, ἡ. ἕκαστος ἀπώλετο Od. 3.87.

ηωθεν.g: [ἠώς + -θεν 1.] From the dawn; hence, at dawn, in the morning. Referring to the next morning: ἠ. ἴτω ἐπὶ νῆας Il. 7.372. Cf. Il. 7.381, Il. 11.555 = Il. 17.664, Il. 18.136, Il. 23.49, Il. 24.401: ἠ. ἀγορήνδε καθεζώμεσθα κιὁντες Od. 1.372. Cf. Od. 3.153, 366, Od. 4.214, Od. 7.189, Od. 12.293, Od. 14.512, Od. 15.308, 506, Od. 17.600, Od. 18.248, Od. 19.320, Od. 21.265, 280, Od. 24.72.

ηωσ.g: -οῦς, ἡ (ἠϝώς) [ἀϝοσ-. Cf. ἠέριος.] Dat. ἠοῖ (ἠόι)̈ Il. 7.331, Il. 11.685, Il. 13.794, Il. 24.600, etc.: Od. 4.407, Od. 12.24, Od. 14.266, Od. 16.2, etc. Acc. ἠῶ (ἠόα) Il. 5.267, Il. 8.565, Il. 9.240, Il. 18.255, etc.: Od. 2.434, Od. 7.288, Od. 16.368, Od. 23.243, etc. Locative ἠῶθι Il. 11.50: Od. 5.469, Od. 6.36. 1 Dawn, the dawn, the daybreak: ἅμʼ ἠοῖ Il. 7.331, Il. 9.618, 682, Il. 11.685, Il. 24.600, ὅσον τʼ ἐπικίδναται ἠ. Il. 7.451, 458, ἠῶθι πρό (in front of the dawn, with the dawn) Il. 11.50: Od. 5.469, Od. 6.36. Cf. Il. 5.267, Il. 7.433, Il. 8.1, 508, Il. 10.251, Il. 23.227, Il. 24.12, 695: Od. 4.194, 407, Od. 6.31, Od. 7.222, Od. 12.24, Od. 14.266 = Od. 17.435, Od. 15.50, 396, Od. 16.2, 270. 2 A dawning or morning considered as a space of time: ὄφρʼ ἠ. ἦν Il. 8.66 = Il. 11.84, ἠοῦς ὄψεαι (in the morning) Il. 8.470, τὸν [μῦθον] ἠοῦς (the morrow's) 525. Cf. Il. 21.111: νηῦς ἠῶ πεῖρε κέλευθον (through the morning) Od. 2.434. Cf. Od. 7.288, Od. 9.56. 3 A morning considered as a point or unit of time or as one of a series: δυωδεκάτη Il. 1.493 = Il. 24.31, Il. 21.80, Il. 24.413. Cf. Il. 13.794, Il. 21.156, Il. 24.781, 785: Od. 19.192, 571. 4 The quarter of the dawn, the east: πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε Il. 12.239: Od. 9.26, Od. 13.240. Cf. Od. 10.190. 5 The dawn personified: ῥοδοδάκτυλος Ἠ. Il. 1.477 = Il. 24.788, Il. 6.175, Il. 9.707, Il. 23.109, Ἠ. ἐκ λεχέων ὄρνυτο Il. 11.1. Cf. Il. 2.48, Il. 8.565, Il. 9.240, 662, Il. 11.723, Il. 18.255, Il. 19.1, Il. 24.417: Ἠοῦς υἱός Od. 4.188. Cf. Od. 2.1, Od. 5.1, 121, 390, Od. 6.48, Od. 9.151, Od. 10.541, Od. 12.3, Od. 23.243, etc.
